title: Share Trading Policy Guide

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chairman. Prior written notification of dealing during a trading window goes to the Chairman of the Board (or his delegate director) and the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman of the Board; prior written notification of dealing during a trading window goes to the Lead Independent Director (or his delegate director) and the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Senior Executives
tiers.description: Executives who are direct reports to the CEO, including key management personnel as defined by accounting standards. The policy's designated-personnel provisions also extend to participants in EVENT's long-term incentive plans (e.g. the Executive Performance Rights Plan) and any other employee notified in writing by the Company Secretary. Notification of dealing during a trading window goes to the CEO (or her delegate director) and the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: other designated personnel
tiers.description: Any other employee determined by the Chairman and/or CEO to be designated personnel and so notified in writing by the Company Secretary. Notification of dealing during a trading window goes to the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Employees (other than designated personnel)
tiers.description: Employees not designated as directors, Senior Executives or other designated personnel. May deal at any time absent inside information, though strongly advised to limit dealing to trading windows; may be temporarily made subject to Section 2 restrictions if given project-based inside information.

tiers.name: Related parties
tiers.description: Spouses or de facto spouses, dependants under 18, and any other party a designated person is deemed to control or significantly influence (e.g. trustee or beneficiary of a trust established by or on their behalf).

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions in products which operate to limit the economic risk of holding EVENT securities

windows.start_anchor: second business day (excluding the day of the trigger event) after EVENT's AGM, the half-yearly results announcement, or the full-year results announcement
windows.end_anchor: end of the 4-week period from the window opening

windows.start_anchor: period determined by the Board and notified to designated personnel following release of price sensitive information the Board considers fully informs the market
commencement of the offer period specified under a disclosure document (e.g. prospectus or PDS) released by EVENT

rules.section: Introduction; 2 Trading windows; Prior notification of trading during a trading window
rules.detail: Securities are defined to include options, rights, derivatives and any other financial product, whether created by EVENT or a third party, so an OTC put/call is caught. Dealing must occur within a trading window, with prior written notification given to the relevant approver and acknowledgement received before dealing; outside a window, discretionary consent (rarely given) is required.
rules.evidence: The policy applies to all EVENT "securities", which includes shares, options, rights, derivatives and any other financial product able to be traded on ASX or another stock exchange, whether or not such securities are created by EVENT or issued or created by third parties.

rules.section: Unvested entitlements and risk limiting products
rules.detail: Absolute ban, overriding anything else in the policy, on risk-limiting products (hedges) over unvested options or performance rights.
rules.evidence: designated personnel must not engage in transactions or arrangements in risk limiting products which operate to limit the economic risk of unvested entitlements to EVENT securities (e.g. hedging arrangements in relation to unvested options or performance rights)

rules.section: Unvested entitlements and risk limiting products
rules.detail: Same absolute ban extends to vested EVENT securities that remain subject to a holding lock or other disposal restriction (e.g. plan trust restrictions).
rules.evidence: or vested EVENT securities that are subject to a holding lock or other disposal restriction.

rules.section: 2 Trading windows; Prior notification of trading during a trading window
rules.detail: Once unrestricted, arrangements in risk limiting products are dealt with the same as any other dealing: limited to trading windows, with prior written notification and acknowledgement (or discretionary, rarely-given consent outside a window).
rules.evidence: Dealings in EVENT securities or entering into transactions or arrangements in risk limiting products should be limited to the trading windows referred to above.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar is a 'financial product' created by a third party in respect of EVENT securities and so falls within the securities definition, subject to the same trading window/consent regime; if structured to limit economic risk it would also be caught as a risk limiting product (prohibited outright on unvested or holding-locked securities).
rules.evidence: any other financial product able to be traded on ASX or another stock exchange, whether or not such securities are created by EVENT or issued or created by third parties

rules.detail: Outright ban at any time, with no consent route.
rules.evidence: Designated personnel are prohibited from engaging in short selling in EVENT securities at any time.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.

CFDs are not named but are a financial product/derivative over EVENT securities and so fall within the securities definition and the general dealing/window/consent regime; a CFD used to hedge unvested or holding-locked holdings would instead be caught by the absolute risk-limiting-product ban.
rules.evidence: which includes shares, options, rights, derivatives and any other financial product

rules.detail: Designated personnel need prior written consent, which the policy states 'will not usually be given' and is only considered in exceptional circumstances, applying even if requested during a trading window.
rules.evidence: Designated personnel must not enter into margin lending arrangements which could result in a forced sale of EVENT securities, unless they have obtained prior written consent (which will not usually be given). Applications for consent will only be considered in exceptional circumstances in accordance with the procedure in paragraphs 015 – 018. This procedure applies even if the request for consent is made during a trading window.

rules.detail: No consent requirement applies to non-designated employees; margin lending is merely discouraged because of the risk of a forced sale while the employee holds or is perceived to hold inside information.
rules.evidence: Employees who are not designated personnel should note that margin lending and other such arrangements are discouraged as they could result in a forced sale of securities during a period when you are in possession of or could be perceived to be in possession of inside information.

rules.detail: Encumbrance is not named as a distinct concept; the only clause touching on granting security over EVENT securities is the margin lending restriction, which necessarily involves pledging shares as collateral for the loan and is therefore subject to the same rarely-granted consent regime.
rules.evidence: Designated personnel must not enter into margin lending arrangements which could result in a forced sale of EVENT securities, unless they have obtained prior written consent (which will not usually be given).

rules.detail: No general 'secured financing' concept is named; only margin lending arrangements resulting in a possible forced sale are addressed, and any loan secured on EVT securities functioning like a margin loan would need the same rarely-granted prior written consent.
rules.evidence: Designated personnel must not enter into margin lending arrangements which could result in a forced sale of EVENT securities, unless they have obtained prior written consent (which will not usually be given).

rules.detail: Absolute ban, overriding anything else in the policy, on short term trading, guided by a six-month intention test; carve-out for immediate sale of shares received on conversion/vesting/DRP.
rules.evidence: Despite anything in this policy, designated personnel must not engage in short term trading of EVENT securities.

exceptions.approver: Chairman, Lead Independent Director or EVENT CEO (or appointed delegate director), as applicable
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship where designated personnel have a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling the relevant EVENT securities

exceptions.approver: Chairman, Lead Independent Director or EVENT CEO (or appointed delegate director), as applicable
exceptions.evidence: designated personnel are required by a court order, or there are court enforceable undertakings (e.g. in a bona fide family settlement), to transfer or sell the EVENT securities or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement to do so

exceptions.approver: Chairman, Lead Independent Director or EVENT CEO, as applicable
exceptions.evidence: any other exceptional circumstance (the validity of which will be subject to the discretion of the Chairman, Lead Independent Director or EVENT CEO, as applicable) in which the proposed dealing is the most reasonable course of action available.

exemption_authority: Consent may be given or refused by EVENT in its discretion without giving any reasons, and can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or circumstances change; a refusal is final and binding and the applicant must keep it confidential. Outside a trading window, consent will generally be refused unless exceptional circumstances (hardship, court order, or another circumstance at the Chairman's/Lead Independent Director's/CEO's discretion) exist.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin lending consent applies even inside a window
bespoke_clauses.clause: This procedure applies even if the request for consent is made during a trading window.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, if it looks like a margin loan capable of triggering a forced sale, cannot simply be timed into an open trading window; it needs the separate exceptional-circumstances consent that is rarely granted.

bespoke_clauses.topic: risk limiting products sweep unvested and locked shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: designated personnel must not engage in transactions or arrangements in risk limiting products which operate to limit the economic risk of unvested entitlements to EVENT securities ... or vested EVENT securities that are subject to a holding lock or other disposal restriction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar can only be considered over vested, unrestricted EVT shares; performance rights, unvested options and plan shares still subject to a holding lock cannot be collared at all, with no consent override.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated personnel must not conduct any dealings or enter into transactions during a trading window until acknowledgement has been received for the notification.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even within an open window, the derivative legs of a collar cannot be executed until written acknowledgement of the notification is received, adding a timing dependency to any bank execution schedule.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no defined secured financing concept beyond margin loans
bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy prohibits margin loan arrangements which could result in a forced sale of EVENT securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because only margin lending (not secured financing generally) is named, a loan structured to avoid the specific features of a 'margin loan' resulting in forced sale may arguably sit outside this restriction, though it would likely still be treated as such in substance by the Company Secretary.

summary: A funded collar is not clearly available, and turns heavily on vesting status and how the loan is characterised. The put and call themselves are 'risk limiting products'/financial products caught by the securities definition: if written over vested, unrestricted EVT shares they can be dealt within a trading window (or, outside one, only with rarely-granted exceptional-circumstances consent) subject to prior written notification and acknowledgement from the Chairman, Lead Independent Director, CEO or Company Secretary depending on tier; hedging of unvested entitlements or vested but holding-locked shares is absolutely prohibited with no consent route at all. The loan, if it functions as a margin lending arrangement capable of producing a forced sale, needs prior written consent that 'will not usually be given' and is considered only in exceptional circumstances, even if sought inside a trading window - this is the most likely blocking point for a bank-secured funded collar. Refusal of any consent is final, confidential, and cannot be challenged, and there is no minimum shareholding carve-out or disclosure regime for secured financing. Overall, the derivative legs could plausibly clear on vested, unrestricted shares within a window, but the secured loan leg faces a strong practical veto.
